input.why: Across their other profiles, mp_triple_sip_soft/normal is their most common choice for the Y button (14 of 35 games, 40%, e.g. 007 - First Light row 43), well ahead of any other pattern for this button.
mp_right_sip_soft with delay_off 250 is their dominant pattern for X (13 of 34 games, 38%, e.g. ARC Raiders row 34), matching Dash's need for a deliberately-held/released trigger.
mp_triple_sip/normal is their clear top pattern for B (14 of 37 games, 38%, e.g. ARC Raiders row 30), well ahead of the next option.
mp_center_sip/toggle is by far their most common binding for left_trigger (19 of 41 games, 46%, e.g. ARC Raiders row 32), consistent enough to carry over for the wall-grab job.
mp_center_puff/normal is their leading valid pattern for right_trigger (11 of 41 games, 27%, e.g. 007 - First Light row 32).
mp_right_puff/delay_on 100 is their dominant left_bumper pattern (15 of 39 games, 38%, e.g. Apex row 39), well clear of alternatives.
mp_right_sip/delay_on 75 is their top right_bumper pattern (10 of 39 games, 26%, e.g. Apex row 38).
mp_triple_puff/delayed_latch 250 is their strongly dominant pattern for left_joy_up (20 of 43 games, 47%, e.g. 007 - First Light row 18).
mp_left_center_sip/toggle is their strongly dominant pattern for left_joy_down (21 of 43 games, 49%, e.g. 007 - First Light row 19).
mp_right_center_sip_soft/tap 250 is their clear top dpad_N pattern (12 of 28 games, 43%, e.g. Apex row 47).
right_puff_soft/delay_on 250 is their leading dpad_S pattern among device-native inputs (8 of 30 games, 27%, e.g. CoD Black Ops 6 row 45).
Among device-native inputs, mp_left_sip/delay_on 200 is their most-used dpad_W pattern (4 of 31 games, 13%, e.g. CoD Black Ops 6 - TEST WZ 2.0 row 47).
mp_left_sip_soft/normal is their clear top dpad_E pattern (12 of 33 games, 36%, e.g. ARC Raiders row 44).

input.summary: Bound the 13 real controller controls (jump/dash primary+alt, all four grab buttons, stick and d-pad movement/aim) to each output's dominant historical pattern, all marked inferred since the evidence is cross-game button usage rather than confirmed same-job bindings. Left unbound: Start, Back, Guide, and the LT+RT+Start chord (no sourced function in Celeste, avoided guessing), plus all keyboard keys and the mouse button (no function on this controller profile). No questions were needed - every control had one historical pattern clearly ahead of the rest.
